title: Overview of 60-Day Free Trial Plans for New SendGrid Accounts
snippet:
Beginning March 25, 2025 and when creating a new Twilio SendGrid account for email sending through either [Twilio Console](http://www.twilio.com) (then navigating to SendGrid) or directly with [SendGrid](http://www.sendgrid.com), users will be given a 60 day timed free trial plan. This trial period provides your team with time to evaluate and test the email offerings of the Twilio SendGrid product before determining if an [Email API and Marketing Campaigns paid plan](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api/pricing) makes sense for your business.
## What You Need To Know
Twilio SendGrid accounts are primarily separated into two main account plan types: "Email API" and "Marketing Campaigns". Accounts on a 60 day timed trial plan will grant temporary access to using both plan types--allowing time to test the functionality of each plan based on your team's needs. Both "Email API" and "Marketing Campaigns" have individual limitations (and can also be upgraded and downgraded independently) during the trial period as follows:

After the 60 day trial period, email send via any web API or SMTP integration for the account will stop unless an appropriate "Email API" plan is chosen before then via "Settings > Account Details > Your Products".

After your account's trial period ends for "Email API" or "Marketing Campaigns", many features will be inaccessible and email send will be stopped unless either package is upgraded to a paid plan. Note that your team will still be able to login to your account with any valid credentials and navigate some of the Twilio SendGrid user interface console without restriction. There will be a banner displayed across the top of the user interface alerting that your trial period has ended.
If your account's trial period (60 days) expires, the following will occur:
**End of "Email API" Trial**
- **Any active email send integration using your account's API keys will stop sending messages**
**End of "Marketing Campaigns" Trial**
- **Any active email send for Marketing Campaigns will stop sending messages**
- **Access to the "Marketing" user interface console will no longer be possible. Important Note: Customers on the free Marketing plan will have access to our Design Library; however, the other subtabs within the Marketing tab will remain inaccessible.**

title: SendGrid Pricing 2026: Essentials, Pro and the Retired Free Plan
snippet:
There is no free plan any more: new accounts get a 60-day trial capped at 100 emails a day.

Twilio retired it in 2025, and the trial that replaced it is the only $0 option left. A [Twilio changelog entry dated May 28, 2025](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/changes-coming-to-sendgrid-s-free-plans) announced the end of the free Email API and free Marketing Campaigns plans: existing free accounts kept their limits for 60 more days, then sending was paused and Marketing Campaigns tools were switched off. Free accounts storing more than 100 contacts had their contacts deleted, with no restore after upgrading.
New accounts have received a 60-day trial instead since March 25, 2025, according to SendGrid's [trial overview article](https://support.sendgrid.com/hc/en-us/articles/35270136965403-Overview-of-60-Day-Free-Trial-Plans-for-New-SendGrid-Accounts). The trial allows 100 emails a day through the API or SMTP, gives access to most Essentials features, and needs no credit card. A separate Marketing Campaigns trial runs alongside it with 100 emails a day and 100 stored contacts.
**When the trial ends, mail stops.** Any integration using the account's API keys stops sending, and support cannot restore sending on its own; only an upgrade does. Put the upgrade date in your calendar on day one, because a password reset flow that silently dies on day 61 is the most expensive way to discover the policy. If you need a permanent free tier for a side project, our [best transactional email APIs](/reviews/best-transactional-email-apis) list ranks the services that still have one.

| Service | Entry paid plan | Free option |
|---|---|---|
| SendGrid | Essentials, 50,000 emails | 60-day trial, 100 a day |
| Resend | Pro, 50,000 emails | Permanent, 3,000 a month |
| Mailgun | Basic, 10,000 emails at $15 | 100 emails a day |
| Postmark | Basic, 10,000 emails at $15 | 100 emails a month, no expiry |

### Is SendGrid still free?
No. Twilio retired the free Email API and Marketing Campaigns plans from May 28, 2025. New accounts get a 60-day trial with 100 emails a day and no credit card, and sending stops when the trial ends unless you upgrade to a paid plan.

title: SendGrid Free Trial (November 2026): Length, Limits & What Happens After
snippet:
SendGrid offers a 60-day free trial of its Email API and Marketing Campaigns, with no credit card required, and when it ends, sending stops until you choose a paid plan. There’s no free SendGrid plan anymore: Twilio retired the old free plans in 2025, so the trial caps you at 100 emails a day and 100 stored marketing contacts. That matters most if you’re a developer testing transactional email or a marketer comparing tools, because for direct sign-ups the trial is now the only free way to try Twilio SendGrid.

| **Detail** | **Trial** | **Notes** |
|---|---|---|
| Length | 60 days | Starts on your sign-up date; available only once |
| Credit card required | No | A payment method is only needed when you upgrade |
| Plans trialled | Email API and Marketing Campaigns | The Email API trial covers most Essentials plan features |
| Send cap | 100 emails a day per product | Email API and Marketing Campaigns have separate daily limits |
| Contact cap | 100 contacts | Marketing Campaigns only |
| Excluded features | Dedicated IPs, subuser management, SSO, email validation | Pro and higher on the Email API |
| After the trial | Sending stops | The Marketing tab locks until you upgrade |
| Data kept | Contacts and single sends aren’t deleted | Reaching them needs Basic or higher |
| Extension | Not published | The trial can’t be restarted |
| Money-back guarantee | None published | Refunds cover only the latest month’s charge, for an account unused that calendar month with no overages or stored contacts |
| Free plan available | No | Retired in 2025 |

When the 60 days are up, SendGrid stops sending for any product you haven’t upgraded:
- **Email API:** any integration using your API keys stops sending messages.
- **Marketing Campaigns:** sends stop and the Marketing tab becomes inaccessible. Contacts and single sends aren’t deleted, but you can only reach them by upgrading to the Basic plan or higher.
- **Your login still works.** You’ll see a banner saying the trial has ended.
According to the [SendGrid free trial article](https://support.sendgrid.com/hc/en-us/articles/35270136965403-Overview-of-60-Day-Free-Trial-Plans-for-New-SendGrid-Accounts), technical support can’t restore sending or Marketing access for you. You upgrade yourself, during or after the trial, under Settings > Account Details > Your Products.

title: Is SendGrid free? Not since 2025
snippet:
SendGrid hasn't had a free plan since 2025: new accounts get a 60-day trial at 100 emails a day, and sending stops when it ends unless you've picked a paid plan. Mailfully's free plan has no end date, and it covers 3,000 emails a month with up to 100 on any day. To keep sending on SendGrid, the cheapest plan is Essentials at $19.95 a month for 50,000 emails.

Free plan facts: Mailfully and SendGrid
| Detail | Mailfully | SendGrid |
|---|---|---|
| Emails a month | 3,000 emails | No free plan |
| Daily limit | 100 emails | 100 emails during the trial |
| At the limit | Sending stops at the allowance, and nothing is billed | Can't exceed 100 a day |
| How long it lasts | No time limit | 60-day trial since 2025, then sending stops |
| Card to sign up | Not needed | Not needed |
| Log retention | 30 days | 3 days |
| Inbound email | 100 a month at a mailfully.app address, counted apart from sends | Included |
| First paid plan | $5 a month for 10,000 emails | $19.95 a month for 50,000 emails |

### The clock runs out after 60 days
SendGrid's trial lasts 60 days, and then the account stops sending unless it's on a paid plan. There's no smaller free allowance to drop down to, which makes the trial a poor home for a side project you mean to keep running.

Is SendGrid still free?No, SendGrid has offered only a trial since 2025. A new account gets 60 days at 100 emails a day without a card.

Can I move to a free plan after SendGrid's trial?No, SendGrid no longer has a free plan, so when the trial ends you either pick a paid plan or stop sending. A Mailfully account can stay on our free plan for as long as 3,000 a month covers what you send.
